statements.text: This project will create good-paying jobs for Hoosiers, expand our tax base, and strengthen the economic foundation for communities across the state. [...] As our country races to lead in artificial intelligence and advanced computing, investments like this ensure we are building that future here at home and delivering new opportunities for hardworking Hoosier families.
statements.venue: Quote in Amazon press release on $15B Indiana data centers

statements.text: When it comes to AI, we are the world's leader in AI innovation and investment. We need to maintain this. We're in a race against China for leadership in this space. Someone is going to win, and it should be us. We've also got to ensure we protect our kids as they go online and make sure that there are some guardrails so you can't have people committing crimes with AI.

Additional energy exploration — but we also have to get the federal government out of the way. I just got a bill passed that reforms NEPA, which has gone way too far. Previously, we were prevented from building pipelines and transmission lines. My bipartisan bill was just voted on last year that will fix that.
statements.venue: Washington Reporter interview (energy costs question, in article on AI and energy)

statements.text:
Hoosiers and their businesses should not be footing the bill for AI data centers.

That's why I'm voting for the Ratepayer Protection Act today. 

If a local community welcomes one of these projects, the builders must pay for the power it uses, not pass the cost to the folks across Indiana.

Democrats just blocked a bill that protects hardworking Americans and Hoosiers from higher energy costs driven by AI data centers.

I never want to hear they care about affordability again. https://t.co/n2p3wTLZrK
statements.quoted:
The Ratepayer Protection Act is simple: data centers should pay their own way. American families, farmers, and small businesses shouldn’t be stuck footing the bill for Big Tech’s energy needs.
 
I brought my bill to the Senate floor to protect ratepayers, but Senate Democrats blocked it from passage.

statements.text: .@NEWSMAX "How do we ensure that no human being is ever harmed by AI, and that this new technology exists to serve us and to make humanity better off, not worse off?" Yakym said. https://t.co/8PHeM35OYU

Senate Democrats just killed a bill to protect Hoosier families from higher electric bills.

Democrats talk about affordability. But when they had the power to make Big Tech AI companies pay their own utility bills, not Hoosiers, they voted AGAINST the Ratepayer Protection Act.

I never want to hear them claim to care about affordability again.
